note.text:
• Colon (:): introduces a list or an explanation: We need three things: courage, honesty and help.
• Semicolon (;): joins two closely linked sentences: Some pupils fight; others report it.
• Quotation marks (“ ”): enclose the exact words someone said: “Tell a teacher,” said Bih.
• Hyphen (-): joins words into one: a well-known counsellor, twenty-one, anti-drug.
• Dash (–): a sharp break or added comment: He refused – bravely – to pay.
• Brackets ( ): extra information: The counsellor (Mrs Ngo) meets students on Friday.

worked_example.problem: Punctuate: “the discipline master said report every case at once”
steps: Capital T; the exact words go inside quotation marks after a comma.
The discipline master said, “Report every case at once.”
worked_example.answer: The discipline master said, “Report every case at once.”

cards.idea: A colon introduces a list or an explanation.
example: Bring three things: a pen, a ruler and an eraser.

cards.idea: Quotation marks surround the exact words spoken.
A hyphen joins words; a semicolon joins two linked sentences.
example: anti-drug club; Some fight; others help.
